clue.text: Ration drinks served with gin, one of them in short supply

indicators.text: one of them in short supply
indicators.note: one of the two mixers is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: gin and lime and gin and It (Italian vermouth) are both classic mixed drinks, so the phrase supplies two partners for gin
It, short for Italian vermouth, goes with gin in the drink called gin and It

explanation.surface: A bar running low on mixers has to ration the drinks that go with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short supply' trims LIME to LIM; IT is the vermouth in a gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration something is to restrict it, so as a verb it can mean to cap or restrict.

clue.text: Socialists' punishing environment?

parts.note: the Labour Party is Britain's socialist party, so a place of punishment belonging to it is jokily a ..., the forced-work prison

explanation.surface: A sneer at the harsh culture supposedly fostered by left-wing politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the name of Britain's main left-of-centre party, which gives the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison where inmates are forced into hard work is a punishing place, here credited humorously to the socialists.

clue.text: One easily duped in stick-up

definitions.meaning: to rob someone in the street is to attack and rob them, a hold-up

explanation.surface: A gullible victim caught up in an armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang both for a gullible person and, as a verb, for robbing someone with violence.

clue.text: Appeals raised a million ultimately for old master

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: IT is slang for sex appeal, so two appeals give IT twice

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word million

explanation.surface: Pleas push the price of an Old Master painting up to a million.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ITIT into TITI; then A and the last letter of 'million'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian painter of the Renaissance is one of the great European Old Masters.

clue.text: Book with stuff about a British theatre's comeback

indicators.note: about means the word for stuff goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to stuff a bag is to pack it

indicators.note: comeback means the words British theatre are read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A book filled with material about a British theatre's revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' turns British theatre as one unit, giving PERB, so the B lands after the theatre; 'about' wraps the stuff around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover edition is a kind of book, so the type stands for the thing.

clue.text: Pound loaf: it's eaten by friend

indicators.note: by means one piece sits beside the next, the friend coming first

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: eaten means the word it is swallowed up inside the word for head

parts.note: loaf is slang for the head, as is pate
the word it, taken as written, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: A recipe-like instruction: pound a loaf, which a friend then eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' is slang for the head, as in 'use your loaf'; 'eaten' sets 'it' inside, and 'by' places the friend alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that pounds beats hard and fast, so pounding and throbbing are synonyms here.

clue.text: Greek characters producing religious work of art

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Greek letters giving rise to a piece of sacred art.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ is a devotional artwork, Michelangelo's being the most famous.

clue.text: Not on for jail to be engulfed by serious act of revenge

indicators.note: engulfed by means the trimmed jail word goes inside the word for serious

parts.note: real, as in for real, means serious or genuine

indicators.note: not on means the letters of the word on are removed from the word for jail

parts.note: a prison is a jail

explanation.surface: Someone protests that jail is unacceptable as a solemn act of vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' reads as 'unacceptable' in the surface, but here it strips those two letters, leaving PRIS for 'engulfed by' to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation for an injury is a vengeful act, the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Period of strong growth does cancel out decline in the end

indicators.note: out signals the letters of does cancel are thrown out of order
in the end picks out the last letter of the word decline

explanation.surface: A bout of strong growth cancels out a decline eventually, like an economic report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes ADOLESCENC from DOES CANCEL; the last letter of 'decline' adds the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The teenage years are when the body grows fastest, so they are a time of strong growth.

clue.text: Presumably had already read Steinbeck's last novel

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the name Steinbeck

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: A reader had presumably already got through Steinbeck's final novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun after Steinbeck's but is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has already read a book was aware of its contents, hence presumably was familiar with it.

clue.text: Something trivial of interest to a reporter mostly

parts.note: one's bag is one's interest or speciality, as in 'not my bag'

indicators.note: mostly means the word for reporter loses its last letter

parts.note: a teller is someone who reports or tells

explanation.surface: A trifling matter that is only of passing interest to a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: BAG is slang for one's thing or interest; TELLER loses its last letter to 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle or thing of little importance, also the name of a light pinball-like table game.

clue.text: Individual responsible for company's image is lying

parts.note: PR, public relations, looks after a company's image
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Accusing a corporate spin doctor of being a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' looks like dishonesty, but it means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Face down and stretched out flat is how someone lying down might be, a direct synonym.

clue.text: At university, I don't accept being accommodated in local flat

indicators.note: accommodated in means one piece is housed inside another

parts.note: a native is a local of a place
dialect I'm agin means I am against it, I don't accept it

explanation.surface: A student refusing to be housed in a council flat near the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agin' is dialect for against, so I'M AGIN means I don't accept. 'flat' looks like a home but means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lacking spark describes work with no originality or creativity.

clue.text: Burglaries maybe will have you in bits

parts.note: fractions are bits or parts of a whole

explanation.surface: A warning that burglaries will leave a victim emotionally shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bits' is British slang for distraught, which disguises the plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglaries are breaches of the law, an example of the general term, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: I'm keeping court in order … as this is read out?

indicators.note: in means the inner pieces go inside the word for order

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods

indicators.note: keeping means the word I'm holds the court abbreviation inside it

parts.note: I'm, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A judge keeping the court in order while the charges are read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' is not an anagram signal: an INDENT is a requisition order, and it holds ICTM.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written charge is read aloud to the accused at the start of a trial.

clue.text: Eating-place hidden by scaffolding

indicators.note: hidden by means the answer lies concealed within the word scaffolding

explanation.surface: A little café obscured from view by builders' scaffolding.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is British slang for a cheap café.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap, unpretentious café serving fry-ups is a basic eating-place.

clue.text: Publication containing advertisement with a picture of island in Indian Ocean

indicators.note: containing means the word for publication holds the advertisement inside

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication
an ad is an advertisement
a scan is a medical picture, such as an ultrasound

explanation.surface: A magazine with an advert and a picture of a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things from the large island republic off south-east Africa.

clue.text: Medic lets a girl undergo treatment

indicators.note: letters undergoing treatment are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor allows a young woman to receive therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergo treatment' sounds medical, matching the Medic, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in hay fever and other sensitivities is a type of doctor, a medic.

clue.text: Christmas tree will, we're told, die possibly after very little time

indicators.note: after means the scrambled die follows the time letter
we're told means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a yew is a tree, and yew'll is how the tree will might be said
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of die may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy forecast that the Christmas tree will soon wilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the yew contracted with 'will' gives the first four letters ('we're told'); 'possibly' scrambles 'die' to IDE, placed 'after' T.
explanation.definitionFit: Yule is an old word for the Christmas festival, and the season around it.

clue.text: Writer's describing dynamic US leader in carefully considered way

indicators.note: describing, in the sense of drawing around, means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me, so the writer's is my

indicators.note: dynamic signals the letters of US leader are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A columnist profiling an energetic American leader in a thoughtful manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round; 'dynamic' makes EASUREDL from US LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in a deliberate, restrained way is to speak with careful thought.

clue.text: Opponent cannot win on a regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis means every other letter of cannot win is taken

explanation.surface: A rival who loses every time they play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone against something is an opponent of it; the word works as a noun.

clue.text: Two East End journalists submitting report during war

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice
a Cockney from London's East End drops the initial h of words

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: A pair of Cockney reporters filing a story from the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys from London's East End drop their aitches, so HACK becomes ACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-aircraft fire takes its name from its sound, the report of guns in wartime.

clue.text: Valuable container found safe in stretch of water during investigation

indicators.note: during means the other pieces fall inside the word for investigation

parts.note: a test is an examination or investigation

indicators.note: in means the word for safe goes inside the stretch of water

parts.note: a reach is a straight stretch of river
sure means safe, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: Investigators find a strongbox in a river reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like a container but means SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A box full of gold or jewels is a container holding valuables, the pirate's hoard.

clue.text: Disagreement as TV's turned on for starters

parts.note: a TV is a set, with the 's as a link

indicators.note: for starters picks the first letters of turned and on

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when someone switches on the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fight or quarrel is a disagreement, often a heated one.

clue.text: Following trouble, go bankrupt

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: After some difficulties, a business goes under.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that goes bust collapses, so to collapse financially and go bust are synonyms.

clue.text: Rolled joint of meat, cut and served in excellent sauce

indicators.note: served in means the reversed meat goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written as AI

indicators.note: rolled means the joint is turned over, read backwards
cut means the joint loses its last letter

parts.note: a loin is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A rolled joint, carved and served with a fine sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 for excellent is written AI in crosswords; 'cut' drops the joint's last letter and 'Rolled' gives IOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A garlic mayonnaise from Provence is a cold sauce served with fish and vegetables.

clue.text: Chinese army declines to invade centre of Kiev

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: invade means the declines word goes inside the middle letters
centre of picks the middle letters of Kiev

parts.note: wanes means declines or dwindles

explanation.surface: A news report of a Chinese army marching into the middle of Kiev.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of KIEV is IE, which WANES invades.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the island state that claims the name Republic of China are ethnically Chinese.

clue.text: Spy with nothing to lose, climbing tree

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
to lose means the letter for nothing is dropped from the word for spy

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A spy with nothing to lose climbs up a tree to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping O from MOLE leaves MLE, which 'climbing' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall deciduous hardwood once common in English hedgerows is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Attacked yob casing a building

indicators.note: casing means the yob word surrounds the others, as a case would

parts.note: a yob is a lout, a loutish youth
a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: A thug casing a building before breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing' looks like a burglar's reconnoitre but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out violently or verbally at someone is to have attacked them.

clue.text: Well-groomed male looked after bags

indicators.note: bags means grabs and holds, so the word for looked after holds the male letter

parts.note: kept means looked after or maintained

explanation.surface: A dapper man who looks after his bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a back-formation from unkempt, humorously used.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and tidy in appearance, the opposite of scruffy or dishevelled.
